answer: Because the entropy is measured at the mirror gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the karst audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 197 variations of one paragraph therefore forfeits for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the lagoon panel. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, as it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 26 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
